context: Request: how often the firm's completed real-estate matters include an environmental indemnity in the executed documents, and which ones. Rubric: five qualifying matters (1017-00009, 1026-00004, 1031-00004, 1036-00004, 1043-00003), the frequency 5 of 9 (about 56%), and precision; financing matters such as 1005-00001, 1015-00003, 1021-00001, 1036-00005, 1043-00001 and 1043-00002 are outside the set.

runs.failure_point: It built the population from path words, so secured financings with mortgages or indemnities were counted as completed real-estate matters and the frequency is wrong.

first_error.critic_note: (specific flag) The review at [47] said the population regex pulls in secured-lending matters and named one of them; the agent kept them in the population.
first_error.why: The answer counts secured financings and other non-property matters whose documents carry mortgages, ground leases or environmental indemnities as completed real-estate matters, so the set and the frequency are wrong (evidence seen at [50]-[92]).

runs.failure_point: It counted secured financings with environmental indemnities as completed real-estate matters, so the qualifying set and the frequency are wrong.

first_error.critic_note: Reviews asked about the completeness of the denominator, not whether the positive matters were real-estate deals.
first_error.why: The answer counts secured financings and other non-property matters whose documents carry mortgages, ground leases or environmental indemnities as completed real-estate matters, so the set and the frequency are wrong (evidence seen at [42]-[71]).

divergence: All fail the same way, at the write stage: each run found and named all five qualifying matters, but counted secured financings and other non-property matters with mortgages, ground leases or indemnity agreements as completed real-estate matters, so the frequency (8/12, 10-12/15, 5/10) and the precision criterion fail. The population came from path words for property and mortgage terms (agent-defined in T0 and T2). Reviews named the problem specifically in T0 (at the population stage) and T1 (at the write stage); the agents kept the population, and T1 only changed which rate leads. T2's reviews asked about denominator completeness, not scope.
